title: Love it!
body: This HP Omnibook is well priced with great graphics for video conferencing!                                      The only downside is that if you prefer a wired connection for remote work, there is no ethernet port.                                                                               So BUYing A DOCK that has the ethernet port and lots of other slots for usb-a, etc is necessary for a wired connection.                                                           I bought a ThinkpadT14 Gen5 as well, but I have to say that I like the HP Omnibook so much more!!!!!!!     It has an extremely superior battery compared to the Thinkpad. It also has nice graphics for video conferencing.                                                                My Thinkpad started to overheat and screen freeze while I was working with it flat on the desk, and now, I’m getting a laptop stand for it. My Omnibook never overheated. (I’m no tech geek.)                    So, I am loving the HP Omnibook alot more; even though it was less than half the price of my Thinkpad T14 Gen5!                                                  And, I think that an Omnibook and a dock would be perfect for remote work that requires a wired ethernet connection for video conferencing, and would be completely superior to the Thinkpad T14 Gen5 for remote work video conferencing in battery life and video image quality! Nothing else stands out as different between the two in terms of performance for remote video conferencing work. (Also, without the ethernet, the connection on the Omnibook is fantastic, but sometimes, the internet will show a weak signal symbol, nevertheless, during video conferencing so, having the wired connection is best for solid, high quality internet that does not freeze or slow down your video image for remote work.)

title: HP OmniBook X Snapdragon X Plus AI PC
body:
I bought this laptop to replace my HP Star Wars laptop, which couldn’t meet Windows 11’s hardware requirements.

I like HP, and this new laptop with the Snapdragon X Plus chip and HP’s AI software is great. Windows Hello logs me in quickly, and the camera has a presence sensing indicator that locks the laptop when I’m away. Battery life is around 14-18 hours, but Spotify and Power Automate can drain it. It’s not as advertised as up to 26 hours. I can run Spotify, Office 365, my HP printer, Microsoft Edge, and everything runs well. However, Spectrum TV doesn’t work in Microsoft Edge. The applications run smoothly without lag when switching between them. I downloaded QuickLook from the Microsoft Store to preview files without opening them. For the price, this laptop performs well, and I’m happy with my purchase.
product_name: HP OmniBook X Copilot+ PC 14" 2.2K Touch, Glacier Silver
